description: Adjudications for near-duplicate candidates: rows from different merge jobs of one cluster, and pairs involving a row added by addenda, whose TF-IDF cosine (requirement_or_question or question plus key tokens) is at least review_threshold. Merges fold rows into the named survivor; distinct pairs stay separate. Every candidate at or above review_threshold in round 0 was reviewed on 2026-09-16; the round 1 addenda candidates were reviewed on 2026-09-16.

merges.reason: Same frozen java-zipinputstream and libarchive-bsdtar compatibility-profile rules stated by two merge jobs.
Same strict 7z supported coder and filter set (COPY/LZMA/LZMA2/BZip2/DEFLATE with Delta and x86 BCJ) and unsupported-coder reporting.
Same rule: omitted ancestor directories are synthesised as recorded Omission resolutions.
Same tar end-marker and trailing-data strictness; survivor also covers dangling extension records.
Same import-mode composition: --preserve requires an exact-version --compat profile and reuses its projection.
Same fact: compatibility and preservation modes exist only for ZIP; tar, 7z and stream sources are strict-only.
Same requirement: device nodes, FIFOs and sockets need explicit (privileged) extraction policy.
Same extensibility seam: unknown recipient stanza types are skipped for matching but stay authenticated; unknown classes fail closed.
Same recover_preserved_source API and its surface.
Same finding: profile numeric parameter values are deferred to SPEC 25.3 and never specified.
Same two-level per-segment key derivation with counter nonces.
Same byte-based legacy format detection order and --from agreement rule.
Same recipient-add semantics: wrap the existing AFK and re-authenticate the envelope.
Same PROGRAM obligation: one external-review dossier (key hierarchy and commitment analysis is part of it).
Same normative extraction and metadata restore order.
Same segment END and ArchiveFinal binding against truncation and reordering.
Same strict ZIP path-safety refusal set.
Same finding: preservation embeds the whole source, roughly doubling archive size.
Same issue: privilege-bearing xattr namespaces (security.*, trusted.*) are captured and restored without a namespace policy.
Same requirement: setuid, setgid and sticky bits must not be restored by default (repo restores them unmasked).
Same finding: dot-slash-prefixed tar members are refused by strict import.
Same ZIP name decoding rules (UTF-8 flag, CP437, Unicode Path extra refinement).
Same requirement: attacker-declared KDF cost is capped and refused before the KDF runs.
Same fact: crypto v1 is INDEXED-only; encrypted STREAM and pipe output are refused.
Same rule: compatibility runtimes are exact-version identifiers with no anonymous default.
Same question: metadata of synthesised ancestor directories and how synthesis is recorded.
Same question: machine-readable output contract, schema publication and stability (canonical JSON rules folded into candidates).
Same question: normative xattr count and value bounds.
Same question: default extraction policy and opt-in surface for dangerous restorations.
Same question: which 7z coders, filters and folder graphs are in v1 import scope.
Same question: handle-based no-follow metadata operations in safe Rust.
Same question: reconciling Research II/III positions (including the NO-GO) with SPEC v1.2.
Same question: the single normative extraction and restore order.
Same question: legacy import budget fields and default values (SPEC 25.1 #23).
